prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Caldera Wildfire Detection and Suppression Support System (WUI). Baseline: segmentation, time sync, health checks; coordination records keep timestamps/participants/radio path; command continuity over automation. Security: Portal named accounts, role auth, MFA else signed expiring emergency credentials; least privilege; config admin separately approved. Append-only audit store; field components buffer/forward signed audit records unmodified. Maintenance record precedes status change. Encrypted retention. No single fault stops operations. Actors: Duty Detection Officer, Air Attack Supervisor, Tanker Base Manager (uses Runway Release Note in acceptance), Helitack Crew Leader (Crewline Mobile Tablet: acknowledgments, location), Drone Pilot Operator, County Emergency Liaison (uses Suppression Drop Receipt for post-incident reconciliation); call signs Redtail, Orion (unmapped). Elements: Caldera Incident Command Portal (Emberhall): common picture, Crew Staging Pin, triage, marks failed radio route impaired (Orion acknowledges), assignment packages; Disconnected Operating Mode (queued updates, no irreversible releases). North/South Lookout Camera Masts: telemetry; North: Thermal Spot Snippet; South: Camera Cleaning Log to Smoke Classifier Module (advisory, human confirmation). Horizon Ridge Drone Dock (Kestrel): Battery Swap Ticket to Drone Pilot Operator. Drone Tasking Service: no flight release; avoids Marigold lanes. Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine (Lantern): detections, Ridge Shadow Mask, rejects unsigned models. MesoWest Weather Fusion Node (Brindle): Wind Shift Bulletin to Redtail. VHF Radio Gateway Repeater (Badger): fallback, queues acks ≥15 min. Talon Air Tanker Dispatch Console (Marigold): blocks incomplete releases; Runway Release Note; Suppression Drop Receipt. East/West Retardant Loading Pumps. States: Confirmed Ignition State, Airspace Restricted State. Training: preseason, comms, qualification, annual refresher, tabletop, live exercise. Governance board (ops, maintenance, infosec, detection/aviation/ground/county reps) approves rollout after residual risk/staffing/baseline/corrective review. Acceptance: Portal, Lantern, Classifier functional tests; Masts, Brindle availability/timing/quality; Drone service/dock field validation (abort, status); Marigold and pumps integration (controls, faults, audit); Badger and Tablet coverage, persistence, auth, degraded ops; Redtail confirms readiness before air ops; state workflows need

New part:
S239: Each after-action review shall reconstruct the timeline from system logs, user accounts, communications records, and maintenance notes without assigning blame to individual operators.
S240: Review facilitators shall document what was expected to happen, what actually happened, why differences occurred, and which corrective actions are necessary before the next readiness cycle.
S241: Corrective actions shall be entered into a controlled improvement backlog with assigned ownership, target completion dates, verification methods, and linkage to the originating event.
S242: Data stewardship shall define retention, access control, quality review, and disposition rules for operational records, sensor data, model outputs, configuration records, and user activity records.
S243: Operational data used for model evaluation shall be protected from unauthorized alteration and shall preserve enough context to support later engineering review and regulatory inquiry.
S244: Changes to the Sentinel Fireline Analytics Engine or Smoke Classifier Module shall be evaluated with representative seasonal data before deployment to confirm that detection performance improves without unacceptable increases in false alerts.
S245: Configuration changes to field equipment shall be versioned, reviewed, and tested in a nonoperational environment before being promoted into the seasonal baseline.
S246: At the end of each fire season, the governance board shall compare system performance, operational workload, maintenance burden, and user feedback against the acceptance criteria approved for that season.
S247: The resulting improvement plan shall define which procedures, training materials, interfaces, algorithms, and support arrangements will be revised before the next seasonal readiness campaign begins.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
